claims.text: CoNiCrFeMn HEA can achieve improved ductility.
An FCC-based microstructure promotes simultaneous twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in CoNiCrFeMn.
Simultaneous twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity help accommodate large strains.
The proposed material may be used as CoNiCrFeMn nanowires or bulk samples.
The proposed CoNiCrFeMn samples have a predominantly FCC phase.
The deformation behavior of CoNiCrFeMn is temperature dependent from cryogenic to elevated temperatures.
Mechanical tensile strain over a range of temperatures activates the proposed twinning and transformation mechanisms.
The FCC phase enables dislocation glide in CoNiCrFeMn.
The FCC phase enables deformation-twin formation and transient HCP-phase formation during deformation.
The synergy between deformation twinning and transformation-induced plasticity reduces dislocation pile-up.
The synergy between deformation twinning and transformation-induced plasticity delays crack initiation.
Reduced dislocation pile-up and delayed crack initiation enhance ductility.
CoNiCrFeMn will have greater strain-to-failure than similar alloys lacking simultaneous twinning and transformation mechanisms.
CoNiCrFeMn will absorb more deformation energy than similar alloys lacking simultaneous twinning and transformation mechanisms.
Standard FCC metals or HEAs without active twinning or phase transformation generally have lower ductility under similar conditions.
Lower valence electron concentration favors FCC stability.
Alloys with higher valence electron concentration or predominantly BCC phase distributions may not exhibit similar ductility.
